archetypes.name: Find the Domain of a Rational Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A rational function is undefined wherever its original denominator is zero, including at values whose factors later cancel.
archetypes.mentalModel: Find every denominator zero before simplifying, then express all real inputs except those values as intervals.

cognitiveTraps.description: Restoring a cancelled denominator zero to the domain after simplifying the formula.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: cancel (x-a) -> a is allowed in domain

cognitiveTraps.description: Omitting one real zero of the original denominator from the restrictions.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: domain excludes only one of two denominator zeros

cognitiveTraps.description: Reporting only the interval between two denominator zeros and omitting valid outer-domain intervals.

archetypes.figureNone: A graph can reveal the excluded inputs directly; the item tests algebraic domain restrictions and uses interval notation.

archetypes.name: Distinguish a Hole from a Vertical Asymptote
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A shared factor creates a removable hole; a zero of the reduced denominator creates a vertical asymptote.
archetypes.mentalModel: Factor first, preserve the original domain restrictions, then inspect the reduced denominator and any cancelled factors separately.
archetypes.governingRelation: cancelled denominator zero -> hole; remaining denominator zero -> vertical asymptote

cognitiveTraps.description: Calling a cancelled common-factor zero a vertical asymptote.
Treating a hole's input as a defined x-intercept after cancellation.

archetypes.figureNone: Plotting the function would disclose the requested hole or asymptote coordinate.

archetypes.name: Find a Horizontal Asymptote
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: For a rational function, the numerator and denominator degrees determine whether its horizontal asymptote is zero or the ratio of leading coefficients.
archetypes.mentalModel: Compare the highest powers: the denominator dominates for a larger denominator degree, while equal degrees leave a constant ratio at large inputs.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reversing numerator and denominator leading coefficients when degrees match.
Using y=0 as the horizontal asymptote when numerator and denominator degrees are equal.

archetypes.figureNone: A graph would show the requested asymptote value directly.

archetypes.name: Describe Local and End Behavior with Arrow Notation
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: One-sided arrows distinguish behavior on each side of a vertical asymptote, while arrows at infinity describe end behavior.
archetypes.mentalModel: Check the sign of the reduced numerator and denominator on each side of a critical input; use distant leading terms for end behavior.
archetypes.governingRelation: x→a− and x→a+ describe distinct sides; x→±∞ describes end behavior

cognitiveTraps.description: Reversing the sign of the function on one side of a vertical asymptote.
Treating the left- and right-hand approaches to a vertical asymptote as the same behavior.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: lim x→a− f(x) = lim x→a+ f(x)

archetypes.figureNone: The item tests the direction of approach; a plotted graph could give away the sign.

archetypes.name: Graph a Rational Function from Its Features
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A rational graph is assembled from domain restrictions, intercepts, holes, vertical asymptotes, horizontal behavior, and one-sided signs.
archetypes.mentalModel: Factor and simplify without forgetting holes, locate intercepts and asymptotes, then sketch separate branches that agree with the arrow behavior.
archetypes.governingRelation: factor → preserve domain → identify hole and asymptotes → intercepts → one-sided and end behavior

cognitiveTraps.description: Drawing a continuous branch through a vertical asymptote.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: graph crosses x=a where reduced denominator is zero

cognitiveTraps.description: Filling a removable hole because the simplified formula is defined at that input.

archetypes.name: Solve an Applied Rational Function Problem
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Applied rational functions model a quantity formed by dividing a changing total by a variable count, rate, or time; domain and units restrict valid inputs.
archetypes.mentalModel: Name the variable and its units, solve the rational relationship for the requested input, then reject values outside the real situation.
archetypes.governingRelation: average rate = total quantity / elapsed time; denominator must be nonzero

cognitiveTraps.description: Multiplying or inverting the given rate incorrectly when solving for time.
Retaining a nonpositive solution for elapsed time.

archetypes.figureNone: A graph is unnecessary for the chosen exact rate calculation and could reveal the target.

archetypes.name: Build a Discounted Average-Cost Rational Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.6 — Rational Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A batch-size-dependent per-unit charge determines total cost, and dividing that total by production count creates a rational average-cost model with a feasible domain.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate the price schedule into a per-unit rate, combine it with fixed and variable batch costs, divide by the count, solve the target equation, and reject roots outside capacity.
archetypes.governingRelation: r(n)=base_rate-discount·n; C(n)=F+n·r(n); A(n)=C(n)/n; solve A(n)=target for feasible n

cognitiveTraps.description: Ignoring the fixed setup fee and matching only the per-unit rate to the target average.
Keeping an algebraic root outside the permitted positive production range.

archetypes.figureNone: The item builds and solves symbolic cost relations; a graph would not clarify the required model construction.
